guarantees.claim: For every share s and register i, int_key_init_qe[s][i] is directly driven by key_init_qe_i[s][i] in combinational logic.
For every share s, register i, and width index j, log_key_init_we[s][i][j] is assigned from int_key_init_we[j][s][i] (index-remapped).
For every share s and register i, key_init_we_o[s][i] is driven by the sp2v_e type-cast of the vector log_key_init_we[s][i].

assumptions.claim: The bit width of sp2v_e must equal Sp2VWidth, and the incoming log_key_init_we[s][i] bit vector must always represent a valid sp2v_e encoding.
assumptions.cond: always, when the generate logic is active
assumptions.risk: A width mismatch or an illegal bit pattern would make key_init_we_o an undefined or corrupted enum value, possibly enabling unintended key-register writes and violating key integrity or confidentiality.

assumptions.claim: The actual dimensions of key_init_qe_i and int_key_init_we must match the generate parameters NumSharesKey, NumRegsKey, and Sp2VWidth so that all array accesses stay within the declared ranges.
assumptions.risk: A dimension mismatch causes wrong signal cross-wiring, potentially omitting or corrupting key-initialization control, leading to skipped key writes or write of wrong share/register.

formal_sketch.consequent: The actual dimensions of key_init_qe_i and int_key_init_we must match the generate parameters NumSharesKey, NumRegsKey, and Sp2VWidth so that all array accesses stay within the declared ranges

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational path from int_key_init_we through log_key_init_we to key_init_we_o does not guard against non-enum bit patterns; a spurious or faulted log_key_init_we[s][i] could cast to an invalid sp2v_e value and silently propagate.
uncertain_points.cond: when log_key_init_we[s][i] does not match any legal sp2v_e member
uncertain_points.risk: An invalid enum on key write-enable may assert writes in unexpected cycles, corrupt key state, or propagate X, weakening key isolation and possibly leaking key material.

security_implications: This block generates key-initialization write‑enable (key_init_we_o) and key data queue (int_key_init_qe) control signals for each key share and register. If the cast to sp2v_e on line 217 receives an out-of-spec value (e.g., through a fault or a rare timing glitch on int_key_init_we), key_init_we_o may take an invalid state that enables a write to a key register at the wrong time or drives undefined simulation/synthesis behavior. Such a mis‑write can overwrite key material with controlled or corrupt data, break key share consistency, or expose key values—directly compromising the AES key security boundary.
